summary: Command injection through incoming message text in macOS desktop notifications
details:
slashvibe-mcp is a Model Context Protocol server for the /vibe messaging service. On macOS it shows desktop notifications for incoming direct messages, mentions, other users' presence notes and posts. It builds an AppleScript command containing the message text and runs it with ``exec(`osascript -e '${script}'`)``, which goes through a shell. The text is placed inside a single-quoted shell argument and only double quotes are escaped.

A single quote in the text ends the shell quoting, so the remainder of the text is interpreted by the shell and can run commands with the user's privileges. The text is written by other users of the service, so another user can trigger this on the recipient's Mac simply by sending a message or setting a presence note. No language model needs to be involved.

Version 0.5.7 runs osascript through `execFile` with an argument array, so no shell interprets the text.

The affected range was established by testing every published release from 0.2.0, the first, to 0.6.x, and spot-checking later releases. 0.5.6 is the last affected release. macOS only.

database_specific.deployer_note: This flaw does not pass through the agent at all, because the message text comes from other users of the service rather than from a tool call, so anyone on the service could run commands on a recipient's Mac by sending a message or setting a presence note, and no agent permission setting would have stopped it. A server that processes content from other people should be reviewed like any other internet-facing software before it is installed on a machine with access to sensitive data. Upgrade to 0.5.7 or later.
